originalTitle: Sebi eases rules on use of depository investor protection fund income
simplifiedContent: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) has made a change to the rules about how some money is used. This money is from a special fund called the Investor Protection Fund, which is meant to protect investors. Sebi is now allowing some of this money to be used for everyday expenses, but most of it must still be kept safe in the fund. This new rule starts in September and has some safeguards to make sure the money is used correctly. This change matters because it affects how the fund is managed and used to help protect investors.

originalTitle: Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide stock market action on Wednesday
simplifiedContent: The Indian stock market went down after four days of going up, because some people sold their shares to make a profit and there were also some worrying signs from other countries. This made investors a bit cautious, especially since they're waiting to see what the US Federal Reserve (or "US Fed") says in its meeting notes. Despite this, technology companies' stocks stayed strong. The market's direction in the short term will likely depend on how well companies are doing, how the monsoon season is progressing, the value of the rupee, and whether foreign investors are putting money into the market. This means that investors are looking at these factors to decide what to do next.

originalTitle: SanDisk shares crash 10% as AI chip selloff spreads to memory stocks
simplifiedContent: SanDisk's stock price dropped 10% recently, and this is likely due to a broader decline in the technology sector, particularly among companies that make computer chips and memory storage. This decline is also affecting other similar companies, such as Micron and Intel, whose stock prices have also fallen. The drop in these stocks may be a sign that the recent excitement and price increases in the tech sector, especially related to AI, are slowing down. This matters because it can impact the overall performance of the stock market and affect investors who own shares in these companies. The decline in these tech stocks, including Samsung, despite some companies reporting profits, suggests a broader market trend.

originalTitle: Gold, silver prices today: Comex gold and silver edge lower amid Middle East tensions, firm US dollar
simplifiedContent: The prices of gold and silver went down on July 7 due to increasing tensions in the Middle East. This happened because when there's uncertainty in the world, the value of the US dollar often goes up, which can make gold and silver less valuable. As a result, the prices of gold and silver futures, which are like bets on what the prices will be in the future, fell sharply. This change in price is important because it can affect the investments of people who own gold and silver. The prices were also influenced by the upcoming release of meeting minutes from the Federal Reserve, which is like a report card on the US economy.

originalTitle: Bust or boom ahead? Here's why Warren Buffett successor's $10 billion bet on big tech has divided experts
simplifiedContent: Warren Buffett's successor, Greg Abel, has invested $10 billion in big tech companies, which has caused some experts to disagree about whether it's a good idea. This investment is notable because Berkshire Hathaway, the company Abel leads, has a large amount of cash - $400 billion - and how it's used is being closely watched. Some experts are skeptical of Abel's strategy, partly because of concerns about artificial intelligence and its impact on the tech industry. This matters because it could affect the performance of Berkshire Hathaway and the overall stock market. The fact that Abel recently bought stock in Alphabet, a big tech company, has added to the debate about his investment decisions.

originalTitle: Rivian shares tumble 15% after EV maker announces 75 million share offering to repay loan
simplifiedContent: Rivian, a company that makes electric vehicles, recently announced that it will sell 75 million shares of its stock to pay back a loan. As a result, the price of Rivian's stock fell by 15%. This means that people who own Rivian stock lost some value in their investment. The company also shared that it made $1.3 billion in revenue in the second quarter, which is a measure of how much money it brought in. The stock sale and loan repayment are important because they affect the company's finances and the value of its stock.
